question: A 33-year-old man living in the United States recently consumed a meal mostly consisting of raw shellfish that his girlfriend brought on her trip to Asia. After 2 days, he experienced a sudden onset of diarrhea and vomiting with severe abdominal cramps while his girlfriend developed mild diarrhea just several hours later. The diarrhea was profuse, looked like rice water, and had a pungent fishy odor. He soon started to experience muscle cramps and weakness, together with a deep labored breathing pattern. They called an ambulance and were transported to a local hospital. Based on the symptoms and blue hue to the skin, the attending physician hospitalized the male patient, started an intravenous infusion, and sent a stool specimen to the clinical microbiology laboratory for analysis. The next day, yellow bacterial colonies were observed on thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose agar (as shown on the image). If you were the microbiologist on call, what kind of bacterial morphology would you expect to see during microscopic evaluation of a gram-stain slide made from those bacterial colonies?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Ingestion of raw shellfish -> foodborne illness -> gastrointestinal symptoms -> 95% CHAIN: Profuse diarrhea with rice water appearance and fishy odor -> cholera infection -> severe dehydration -> 90% CHAIN: Muscle cramps, weakness, and deep labored breathing -> electrolyte imbalance -> metabolic acidosis -> 85% CHAIN: Blue hue to the skin -> cyanosis -> tissue hypoxia -> 80% CHAIN: Hospitalization, IV fluid infusion -> supportive care for dehydration -> stabilization -> 85% CHAIN: Stool specimen sent for analysis -> bacterial culture on thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose agar -> yellow bacterial colonies -> 90% CHAIN: Yellow bacterial colonies on agar -> gram-stain slide preparation -> microscopic evaluation -> Corkscrew-shaped rods -> 95%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of the patient with symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting, muscle cramps, weakness, and deep labored breathing after consuming raw shellfish, along with the growth of yellow bacterial colonies on thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose agar, the likely causative agent is Vibrio cholerae. Gram-staining of Vibrio cholerae would typically show comma-shaped rods.
